attribution: Brewing-prepared adjuncts (flaked/torrified) use published brewing extract figures. Raw grains and rices have no brewing datasheet, so their PPG is derived from USDA FoodData Central nutrition data via lib/fermentable-math.ts — PPG = 46 x (total carbohydrate - fibre) / serving weight. fermentables.name: Flaked Maize
fermentables.description: Pre-gelatinised corn flakes; lightens body and colour and dries the finish without cereal-mashing.
fermentables.usageNotes: Needs diastatic base malt to convert — no enzymes of its own.
fermentables.attribution: Briess retired briess.com/malt/<slug> (all 404) and its replacement brewingwithbriess.com/product/<slug>/ 301s to the catalogue rather than a product page — so the citation now points at the Product Information & Specification Bulletin PDF, which is the actual primary datasheet and carries the typical analysis: extract dry basis, colour in SRM, moisture, protein and diastatic power in Lintner. Each PDF was fetched and confirmed before being written.
fermentables.diastaticPowerNote: Unmalted starch. It has never been germinated, so it brings no meaningful amylase of its own and contributes nothing to the enzyme supply — every point of gravity it yields has to be converted by the diastatic power of the malt beside it. Recorded as zero rather than left blank precisely because it is not unknown: leaving it blank would let a 70%-corn bourbon mash look like a grist whose enzyme balance nobody could assess, when in fact it is the case the assessment exists for.
